senses.gloss:
Pināka
------------------------------------------
The various deities of the Hindu pantheon have certain objects held in their hands—including some weapons—as distinguishing marks.
Though शिव has the त्रिशूल (the trident) as the distinguishing weapon, he also has a bow called ‘Pināka’ which he uses occasionally as in the destruction of त्रिपुर or the three cities of the demons, and the sons of तारकासुर like Tārākṣa.
According to one version, शिव’s trident once fell down and got bent into the shape of a bow. This came to be known as the पिनाक. पाशुपत is the chief arrow that is discharged from this bow.
The word is sometimes defined as ‘that which protects’ (= pāti, rakṣati) people from evil forces.
See also ŚIVA.
